rows.what the ink shows: Two curved parentheses enclose a small rounded a with a right descending exit stroke. The enclosed oval and exit are visible despite the pale folded paper.

Between the two parenthesized labels the fold carries separated dark hooks, short slanting strokes and a few dot-like remnants on two levels. No continuous pair of word bodies or discriminating letter sequence survives the light and crease.

The enclosing left and right curves are visible; the interior has two short right-facing rounded lobes. A tall b ascender cannot be separated securely from the pale surrounding strokes, leaving b versus 3 unresolved.

The tall initial P loop, short r shoulder, low o body and deep final p descender can be followed through the cancellation. No distinct abbreviation point is secure after the p; the isolated dark fleck lies below and to its left.
After Soit, a thick horizontal deletion covers almost the whole short word. Its left upturn and right triangular peak remain, but the intervening u and n bodies cannot be individually distinguished.

Below the inserted Si, the cancelled form retains a tall bent S with a lower return and a separate short i stroke and dot. These two letter positions remain distinct above the cancellation, and the upper inserted S supplies a local shape comparison.

An opening parenthesis is distinct at the left of the cancelled fragment. Several tall stems and low turns follow beneath the horizontal crossing, but the rightmost bodies run into the page edge and do not separately establish all of hilbert.

The first group has tall h/l/b-like rises and a dot above the deletion; the next starts with a clear N and a short crossed ascender. The horizontal strike merges most low letter bodies, including the proposed endings and que, so the complete phrase remains uncertain.

Immediately before the fixed parenthesized e_J, two small rises project above the crossing and broken low hooks remain below it. Their joins and word divisions are covered by the continuous strike, so no two-word reading is secured.

After the parenthesized group, a shallow lower curve and two short upright remnants survive near the right end. Two almost horizontal cancellation strokes cross the bodies, so those remnants do not distinguish a three-word reading.

The cancelled middle line begins with two tall narrow strokes and a low rightward return. Its later baseline is crossed by a heavy straight strike and large zigzag loops; neither the full Nous body nor the proposed allons and se can be secured separately.

At the right of that cancelled middle line, small low humps and a short rising terminal remain before the uncancelled dans. The broad zigzag and horizontal strike merge with the letter bodies and hide both a word boundary and any discriminating continuation.

The bottom cancelled line has a compact tall cluster at its left and low rounded fragments to the right. A heavy rising-and-falling cancellation stroke closes or covers their counters, so I cannot distinguish the proposed o, n and separate a as three underlying bodies.

A short ascender and a crossed upright precede the bracketed region; inside it, low dark bodies and a right-hand descending j-shaped loop survive. The straight strike merges the baseline letters and first index, while a large cancellation return overlaps the opening curves: the full det, both baseline a letters, indices and opening-parenthesis count cannot all be independently secured.

The initial upright/open-right curved capital resembles this page's C in Corollaire. The middle has a raised looped d and separate high accent after the dotted i position; the late horizontal segment belongs to the compressed ending before the comma, and no internal hyphen separates two words. These strokes support Considérons over Bornons-nous.

A tall looped l and separate raised apostrophe are clear at the beginning. The following on lies on the thick strike; a later oval and high dot suggest ai, but the underlying connections and final t remain merged with the cancellation, so the remainder stays uncertain.

After the suggested ait group, a small left oval and an upright crest survive above the long dark baseline, followed by a low terminal stroke. Cancellation covers the intervening bodies and spacing, leaving no secure two-word transcription.

The old lower-right index is covered by a dense black deletion, with only a raised dot surviving; its body and letter count are not recoverable. Beneath it is a separate dotted short i, clearly enclosed by a thin continuous oval, so both correction layers are retained; the ellipsis denotes editorially unknown ink, not written dots.

One baseline a has a visible left oval and right stem. The lower-right index region is crossed by broad black strokes and a loop; these leave an upright remnant but do not securely distinguish both separate i and j bodies from the cancellation.

A left upright fragment, an isolated dot and a second short upright remain above the heavy horizontal cancellation. The initial s/o bodies and terminal crossbar cannot be separated from that stroke, so the whole proposed word remains uncertain.

The deleted word has a looped d, a separate raised apostrophe immediately after it, a small o bowl, and a low u-shaped ending with a separate raised grave-like mark. The apostrophe and accent discriminate d’où from donc despite the strike through its baseline.

The mark after Hadamard is a dark vertical body with two left-facing loops and a crossed upper tip. No detached lower dot can be identified, so the enlarged ink does not securely establish an exclamation mark.

The faint word begins with disconnected small dark bodies and ends with two taller uprights followed by long low exits. The initial c/r and intervening bodies are not distinct enough to count the proposed letters, and no g descender is securely visible to decide rectangle against construit.

The opening capital A and later tall t survive, but the intervening small bodies, following au/un humps, and the compressed bodies of théorème and préambule are too faint to secure those complete words. The final word on the first marginal line has a descending p, rounded low continuation and r exit, supporting pour outside uncertainty.

After the proposed préambule are two separated punctuation-like traces and a faint descending p-like initial, followed by broken low arches and a separate long terminal body. Enlargement and rotation do not recover the small middle letter forms needed to distinguish such possibilities as préciser or prouver.
